response: oh absolutely! i've got a similar thing with data. might sound weird, but I get this strange sense of satisfaction from sifting through a giant mess of numbers and making sense of them... drawing connections... finding patterns. it's like a puzzle and i'm a sucker for it. and there's no better feeling than when you've finally cracked it and everything just clicks into place. it's almost zen-like, keeps me sharp and on my game. some folks meditate, I... wrangle data i suppose. cheers for asking, mate.

question_asked: Lately my 4-year-old nephew has been showing a lot of interest in animals. It’s adorable how he tries to imitate the sounds they make. Even at his tender age, he seeks more and more facts about animals. It reminds me a lot of the time I spent in the school library going through encyclopedias, learning something new every day. Isn't it fascinating how kids are naturally inclined to explore and learn at such a young age? Do you also have any experiences of watching someone show interest in a subject and grow in knowledge overtime, perhaps in your professional field?
response: oh, kids and their endless curiosity, right? there's this young fellow, fresh outta college who got hired at our firm. i mean he knew the basics, but the eagerness was unmatchable. watched him diving into drafts, model building, seemingly trivial stuff you might say, but the way layers, lines, volumes started coming to life, you could tell he's onto sth big. and the sheer amount of sketchbooks he filled with scribbles and drawings, each revealing a progress. Reminds me of the time when i had the same energy. now, it's moar about round table discussions, refining those drafts to align w/ code compliances, client desires and whatnot. Still mesmerizing to see this integral part. Glorifies the saying "learning never goes in vain" indeed.

question_asked: Every once in a while, I like to pick up my old guitar and just strum a few chords. Music has always been my escape, my little island of serenity in the vast ocean of life's responsibilities. I remember during college, we even made a small band and performed in the local pubs. Those were some memorable days. How about you? Do you have any hidden talents or hobbies you occasionally indulge in?
response: ah, those good ol' days. i've always found solace in the stars, mate. just sitting on my terrace on clear nights and staring at the infinity above. never thought of it as a 'talent', but i guess knowing the constellations and understanding the cosmic dance does put me in a pretty exclusive club, huh? 😉 and never mind the reddit rabbit hole i frequently disappear into, haha! don't have a band story to top yours though, just a man and his telescope having a quiet conversation with the universe. 🌌🔭 and oh, discussing physics till the wee hours, that usually puts people to sleep, not sure if it counts as a 'hidden' talent.🤣✨🌌🚀

question_asked: On the internet, you come across so many different types of content. As an amateur photographer, I enjoy spending a chunk of my free time watching photography tutorials and reading camera reviews. There's so much innovation in tech, it's hard to keep up! What's your take on how much technology changes affect your day-to-day life? Is there any particular innovation that you find revolutionizing?
response:
oh man, tech changes? those things just turn the heat up in my life, for real. sometimes i feel like i'm just constantly juggling, y'know? like trynna keep one eye on a pot on the stove, another on some oven roast. all while chopping veggies! lol 

but then tech comes in with these amazing time savers, right? like i've been checking out this sous vide thing, seen that? you just seal up your food, set the temp and forget about it. game changer, i tell you! when it's done, the result is just...ambrosial, no fear of overcooking or nothing. i can spend my time worrying about other things while this sous vide thing wor af its magic. its like having an extra pair of hands around the kitchen, dude... totally revolutionizing my everyday hustle.

but hey, tech ain't all good tho... like all this social media hustle? can't keep up, man. reddit is my sanity island in this tech typhoon lol. trying to keep track of every other platform just fries my brains worse than overcooked tapioca, bro.

question_asked: I've noticed that understanding different cultures and languages has really been valuable in my line of work, it opens up more work opportunities and facilitates communication in such a global world we live in. I've been considering starting to learn a new language but can't quite decide on which one. In your experience, what language would be valuable to learn next, considering your line of work and why?
response: oh, languages... such a tricky beast. currently brushing up on my english skills (and occasionally portuguese) since, y'know, enduring those painfully long boardroom meetings and distilling them into something palatable often means wrestling with english. had spanish as my mother tongue (obviously) helped a fair bit, but international dealings are often english all the way, and those south americans love their portuguese, haha. Swiss army knife in the global business park, that's the endgame here. what do you think? french any good? or should I tackle german? you gotta use every tool in the shed!

question_asked: I've been trying to maintain my posture lately. As a violin teacher, I keep reminding my students about it, and sometimes forget about myself. I realized how important it is to have a good physical condition when playing a musical instrument, and to do that, you have to keep on top of your health in general. What about you? Do you have any activities that you're passionate about and do they require you to maintain good health too? If you don't mind sharing, I'm all ears.
response: oh definitely, mate. i totally understand what you mean. posture really makes or breaks your game, doesn't it? for me, tho, it's different. tbh, i don't perch like a bird on a violin, lol...rather, i'm grounded, feet steadfast on the concrete, flicking through an aisle of candies, doodads, and whatnots, you know? anyway, if we're talking passions here, the internet is my sweet symphony! got a soft spot for delving deep into subreddits! helps me keep in touch with the world outside my modest metropolis, lol. health-wise... apart from the constant threat of carpal tunnel from excessive scrolling, can't say it's much of an issue. but still, try to squeeze in some yoga between shifts and threads, keeps me from turning stiff as a board, ha.

question_asked: I'm lucky that working at home has become the norm for me, being able to make my own schedule and manage my own tasks gives me a sense of control. Helps average out the workload and reduce the stress, you know? How do you usually handle managing tasks at your workplace. Do you have any special software or tool you use, or it's more like an old-school approach with just checklists and reminders?
response: oh man, it's a bit of both for me.. i tend to start the ol' analog way with scribbling in a notebook. helps me think, doodling sorta brings out the creativity, hehe.. but for organization, yeh, gotta go digital. i rely heavily on design software that also allows for project tracking and stuff. helps lessen the chaos, when you're juggling a bunch of different visuals, concepts and timelines! what 'bout you, you got a fave productivity tool?

question_asked: I've been enjoying photography as a hobby recently, and I've managed to sell a few of my snapshots as stock photos online. It's not much money, but it brewed the idea in me that there might be potential in turning this hobby into a side job, or maybe even a full-time gig. How about you, do you personally find that hobbies/talents can potentially be monetized in today's digital era, and have you ever tried it?
response: oh most definitely, the internet provides such a broad platform to get visibility for your art. u do have to be careful tho coz often platforms take quite a bit of profit. i myself tried selling some of my educational resources online, that i developed during my time as a high school principal. there's a surprising market out there for lesson plans, study guides, that sort of stuff. it's not a lot of money, but hey, every bit helps lol ... remember that time is also a resource, don't undervalue your effort. go for it and good luck!

question_asked: I recently tried my hand at learning the piano again. I have an old keyboard at home and thought, why not? Ran into quite a few obstacles as I tried to re-educate myself though. Reading the sheet music was like trying to decode hieroglyphics but I definitely found the instrument therapy, kind of like a different language of expression. Besides the usual things, do you have any unusual ways of expressing yourself? Maybe through writing, art... or perhaps even music?
response: of course, why not! i've found my own time in the kitchen to be the most therapeutic. it's a creative space, ya know? like an easel for a painter. experimenting with different ingredients, shaping dough, even the sizzle sound of a cooking pan... it's all a form of expression for me, where i chisel out my thoughts and feelings into edible works. i think the whole process of selecting ingredients, designing a menu & then finally bringing it all to life on a plate, is pretty much like writing a novel. maybe i'll learn the piano next, who knows! make some kitchen concerts a thing eh? :D

question_asked: Fitness has been a major part of my life for a while now, love the feeling of accomplishment after a good workout. I just set up my new indoor bike and boy, assembly definitely was not the highlight! Makes me appreciate people who do this on a regular basis. What about you? Have you ever had to assemble something complex or do you prefer to let others handle the manual labor?
response:
haha, tell me about it! bought this super expensive swiss ergonomic office chair a while back, even the packaging was heavy. the assembly instructions were this thick booklet, felt like they had written "war and peace" on how-to-assemble this darn thing. one step involved an allen wrench in uncomfortable positions... and let's not start with the 'slide it but do not force it' parts. truly humbling experience.

gotta say though, it did give me a sense of achievement once it was done, sitting on it felt like conquering mount everest. but oof! wouldn't be volunteering to assemble anything in the near future for sure, guess some of us are more born to handle spreadsheets than Allen wrenches :P

question_asked: It's a wild feeling when I think back to my old days working night shifts at a restaurant. I was a line cook for a few years before moving up to a junior chef role. Those were some crazy times — adrenaline pumping, high energy environment, all about the perfect timing and patience. It surely was a school of hard knocks for me, learned a lot about people and life during those days. Cooking's still a beloved hobby of mine. How about you? Got a hobby, an art, or activity that's been a teacher in the school of life to you?
response: Oh absolutely, every day is a learning experience for me too in its own unique way. Being a graphic designer kinda goes hand in hand with my love for visual arts. It's not just a job, y'know? Every project, every client I work with, it's sorta like a story unfolding, teaching me something new way about how to perceive the world and translate someone's vision into a design. Though I must say, there have been some... let's say “challenging” clients throwin' me a curveball or two with their demands lol... but getting through those projects... ah, the satisfaction. it's worth it. I also find some solace in trawling thru subreddits about creative design and arts, kinda keeps me motivated and inspired, y'know? Sure I don't have the adrenaline pumping scene of a restaurant kitchen (kudos to you for that, mate), but the gentle dance between creativity and technicality in my life as a designer... can't say I would trade it for anything else. Each day, each project is a new lesson in the big ol' school of life.

question_asked: I've been thinking about my school days lately, and how my programming teacher always used to tell us: "Coding languages are like tools, each has its purpose and best use case scenario." He really pressed us on learning more than just one language. So I got into Java, Python, and even a bit of R, trying to diversify my skill set. Did you also venture in coding back at school or maybe later on in life? What has been your experience in juggling more than one skill?
response:
oh definitely, I totally relate to the juggling part but in a bit of a different setting. in a former life, did lots of juggling with different tasks that required adaptability and a fair bit of dedication (had me around the clock, ugh). i remember having a go at coding once, it was years ago... didn't stick with me, haha. 

these days, my online kicks come from the social sphere, diving into the endless rabbit holes of reddit, getting lost in discussions and debates. i'm more comfortable in a pair of scrubs rather than coding languages, tbh. anyway, kudos to you for managing all those languages, sounds like quite a feat.

question_asked: So, you know what's funny? My best friend was getting a new fridge delivered. He's a software developer, so he was tracking the delivery truck in real-time via the app. And then, out of nowhere, the whole thing goes offline. He has no clue where the truck is or when his fridge will arrive. He was forced to spend the whole day at home, not knowing when exactly the delivery will happen. Do you ever have to wait at home for packages like this because the tracking apps or services aren't reliable? The technology is impressive when it works, but super frustrating when it doesn't, right?
response:
oh man, u've hit a nerve here!! I'm a data scientist, right, so i deal with apps and real time data every damn day at work and it's super frustrating when I can't have the same smooth experience in my personal life. I recently tried using a new grocery delivery service here in Dublin. Promised a 2-hour delivery window. Yeah, right... 

First time, they tell me they can't deliver my order, after I kept myself free for the evening for it. Second time, try to get something delivered, and their real-time tracking goes off the grid! Then I get a call an hour later from the delivery guy asking for directions.

Sometimes it's just plain old bad luck, thinkin' the tech is just out to 'get me' after i have spent the whole day wrangling data. You'd expect it to be more reliable in this day and age, wouldn't ya? Especially when u're keen on waiting on some good Irish cheddar or those irresistible Taytos, haha. I mean we've put a man on the moon, we should be able to keep track of a delivery inside of Dublin city. Looks like my personal and professional lives are both haunted by data reliability issues :D But hey, keeps the job interesting ... and frustrating at the same time!

question_asked: Just the other day I was speaking to my next-door neighbor about his job. He's a writer and he was telling me about the writer's block he was experiencing. He was drowning in a sea of words, or lack thereof, trying to pen the perfect chapter for his book. Can't say I'd enjoy that! I guess there can be challenging parts in every job. What's the most challenging part of yours, or perhaps something you're currently dealing with?
response: haha tell me 'bout it... i mean, imagine trying to explain calculus to a teenager who'd rather be on tiktok. makes writer's block sound like a walk in the park! but hey, seeing that "aha!" moment when everything clicks is kinda worth all the teeth pulling. and right now, exam season's on the horizon, which means stacks of papers to grade... but hey, just another day at the office, amirite? :D

question_asked: As much as I consider myself an introvert, I have to say, at times, I enjoy engaging in public speaking or having conversations on intriguing topics. At one of the recent webinars, I had a blast talking about the evolution of technology in our everyday life. I was utterly surprised by the diverse views from the attendees, especially from those who were deep into the tech world. Online discussions like these can be a well of knowledge, right? Have you ever participated in webinars or conferences in your field, and if so, what was the most exciting thing you learned recently?
response: oh totally get you, being a bit of an introvert myself... but get me started on a topic i'm excited about (like the rapid evolution of tech in business - seriously, who isn't geeking out in this day and age!), and i'm practically a chatterbox haha :D. as a business development manager, i take part in conferences quite regularly, but with the whole pandemic, it's been webinars galore. recently, I attended a virtual seminar about digital marketing trends and guys, the stuff i learned is nothing short of revolutionary. like, ever think about how 'voice search' is gaining momentum? apparently 20% of mobile queries are voice searches. wild, right? makes me think about all the potential strategies in my field to capitalize on this trend. it's a brave new world out there, friends ಠ_ಠ.

question_asked: I just picked up a new hobby recently - photography. It's so fascinating how you can play with lights and shadows, and capture a perfect moment that you can appreciate forever. The only annoying thing is, sometimes I have a great shot in mind, but it just doesn't translate well into the image. I imagine it's a lot like many other creative processes, where there's this gap between the imagination and the final product. Have you ever experienced something like this in what you do?
response: haha oh man, do I know that too well. pretty similar stuff here. for instance there are times when i'm trying to create something (on my computer, wink wink), and the idea in my mind just not lining up with what's coming out on the screen, gets frustating for sure. oh and then those bugs popping up from nowhere, just like unwanted noise in your shot i guess :D but it's all part of the game, as they say. gotta keep cracking at it until the final product is as close to the initial idea as possible. photography sounds pretty rad though, keep at it!

question_asked: I recently helped my friend move his restaurant business online in response to the pandemic, and it's been quite a learning curve dealing with all the logistics and tech stuff! Especially when issues pop up, like the website crashing or customers not being able to place their orders, or when the delivery service messes up. Drives him crazy sometimes! Anyway, have any recent situations challenged you to venture into something you're unfamiliar with?
response: oh definitely! not sure if you're familiar with the environmental policy changes that have popped up recently but let me tell ya... it's been a thick wad of paperwork to get through. just when I thought I had my head around one set, the next one turns up. plus, have to google a ton of legal jargon. for sure not what i signed up for when i decided to major in enviro sciences! on the bright side though, i've gained a newfound appreciation for the law sector. they really know how to write doozies 😅 but yeah, kinda feels like hopping into cold water when you ain't used to swimming that much, if that makes any sense? lol, always a challenge figuring out something new, right? but it's part of the thrill, keeps things fresh n interesting. 👩‍💻📚

question_asked: Hey, I'm a bit of a bookworm and I've been really getting into self-published books recently. The authors' passion for their craft is palpable and their creativity is off the charts. It's making me consider writing a book of my own! I'm a fan of fantasy and crime fiction. Do you have any interest in literature or writing? If you were to write a book, what would it be about?
response: aha! umm i do scribble a bit sometimes, usually end up concocting some sort of mystery about missing celestial bodies. sounds wild right? i guess it comes with the territory when you spend most of your nights looking up at the sky! if i ever write a book, it'd probably be something like "the Case of the Vanishing Nebula" or some other astronomical who-done-it. i'm not the best at character arcs or romance sub-plots haha, so will stick to what i know! proper old-school space oddity! anyone else out there a fan of space whodunits? :D

question_asked: I'm missing the good old school days. I used to enjoy the brainstorming sessions and group work for project assignments. The failing and trying again, it was all fun, educational and so much within your control. I wonder whether working adults enjoy the same. Like, what are your thoughts on working in a team, especially if it's a challenging project that involves lots of problem-solving? Got any interesting or frustrating experiences to share?
response: oh boy, do i have stories! working as a chef, team work is basically the bread and butter, kinda like how the pasta is to the bolognese sauce, you know? when it's rush hour and you've got to feed a restaurant fulla famished customers, you gotta rely on your sous chefs, line cooks and everyone in between like your life depends on it. we got interesting dynamics, especially in an italian kitchen. i remember when our supplier messed up the delivery of the buffalo mozzarella for the caprese salad on the busiest night, it was a bunch of chaos, dealing with that was... quite something! :D on one hand, you got everyday challenge of bridging the communication gap let's say amongst front of house and the kitchen, so many egos and personalities. So yeah, glaring at them for sending back a dish or letting them know the wait time isn’t too long, there is quite a tangle. but then again, seeing customers smile after a well-made dish? 100% worth it. don't regret a single moment of stress in this profession, despite the frustration :]
